purpose: AI-COST-001 public-literature map for quantum/hybrid AI training cost reduction

sources.title: A quantum algorithm for training wide and deep classical neural networks
sources.authors: Alexander Zlokapa, Hartmut Neven, Seth Lloyd
sources.relevance: Reports logarithmic-in-training-set-size complexity for a specified wide/deep-network setting under efficient quantum linear-system, state-preparation and readout conditions; the paper itself states these conditions are required for end-to-end exponential speedup.
sources.boundary: Not a demonstration of general frontier-model training cost reduction on real hardware.

sources.title: Quantum algorithms for feedforward neural networks
sources.authors: Jonathan Allcock, Chang-Yu Hsieh, Iordanis Kerenidis, Shengyu Zhang
sources.relevance: Provides training/evaluation algorithms with potential quadratic network-size dependence improvement while relying on quantum memory/data-access primitives.
sources.boundary: Asymptotic algorithmic result; not end-to-end infrastructure economics.

sources.title: Backpropagation scaling in parameterised quantum circuits
sources.authors: Joseph Bowles, David Wierichs, Chae-Yeun Park
sources.relevance: Identifies structured parameterized circuits with gradient-estimation scaling approaching classical backpropagation and reports about two orders of magnitude training-cost reduction on a 16-qubit toy classification example.
sources.boundary: Not a frontier-AI or end-to-end cost demonstration.

sources.title: On quantum backpropagation, information reuse, and cheating measurement collapse
sources.relevance: Shows a key obstacle to backpropagation-style information reuse in quantum models and identifies conditions involving multiple state copies for matching backpropagation scaling.
sources.boundary: Barrier/interface result, not a cost advantage claim.

sources.title: Barren plateaus in variational quantum computing
sources.relevance: Documents exponentially suppressed gradients as a major trainability barrier and surveys causes/mitigations.
sources.boundary: Review evidence; does not establish a practical AI-training advantage.

sources.title: Does provable absence of barren plateaus imply classical simulability?
sources.relevance: Collects evidence that structures avoiding barren plateaus can in many cases also enable classical simulation, creating a critical advantage-vs-trainability gate.
sources.boundary: Case-by-case evidence, not a universal no-go theorem.

sources.title: Resource-state quantum RAM for fast and error-correctable queries
sources.relevance: Recent QRAM architecture relevant to coherent classical-data access, a prerequisite/cost center for many QML algorithms.
sources.boundary: QRAM architecture progress is not evidence of cheap end-to-end AI training.

sources.title: A rigorous and robust quantum speed-up in supervised machine learning
sources.relevance: Establishes an end-to-end quantum speedup for a constructed supervised classification problem with classical data access.
sources.boundary: Task-specific learning advantage; not general neural-network training economics.

sources.title: Advantage of quantum machine learning from general computational advantages
sources.relevance: Shows how general quantum computational advantages can induce supervised-learning advantage for carefully defined task families.
sources.boundary: Does not demonstrate practical frontier-AI training or the UQPU cost moonshot.

research_boundary: Public literature contains important conditional, task-specific and architectural routes, but this audit found no evidence establishing a general 100,000,000x, billion-fold or tens-of-billions-fold end-to-end reduction in practical frontier AI training cost.
